The pore characteristics of this sample were measured by 77K N porosimetry and the pore size distribution is provided in Figure 23b, revealing 2 that the SBA-15 was truly embedded in the structure and that the washing procedure worked. When compared based on available pore volume, the porous electrospun fibers had approximately 59% of the original pore volume of SBA-15, indicating that the loading is close to the theoretical expectations. Still, the fibers did not appear entirely uniform in shape, with agglomeration appearing throughout the batches of fibers even after the fabrication protocols were updated. 28 a ) b ) Figure 23. A recent batch of fibers a) viewed under SEM and b) demonstrating available pore volume after washing by 2 different methods. After watching the electrospinning process to determine if there was a problem occurring during the fiber fabrication, it was found that there was a glob forming at the tip of the nozzle on the coaxial spinneret shown in Figure 24a. It was hypothesized that the core & shell solutions were blending before becoming electrospun fibers, being the likely cause of agglomeration & nonuniformity seen throughout all the previous fiber batches, as demonstrated in Figures 22a and 23a. Once this problem was mitigated by paying more attention to the solutions flowing from the nozzle tip during the startup of the electrospinning process, a small batch of fibers were able to be prepared with a much more uniform diameter, as shown in Figure 24b. Figure 24. a) Image of a glob forming at the tip of the nozzle of the coaxial spinneret noticed during electrospinning and b) SEM image of uniform fibers produced after preventing glob formation. The fiber fabrications were still being optimized to ensure that the silica substrate, SBA-15, was being properly encapsulated within the fibers. After varying the electrospinning conditions (voltage, flow rate, collector plate distance), batches of fibers that possessed a core-shell structure were not reproducible. From literature reports, it was determined that the polymer concentration in solution and the solvent plays a significant role in the process, especially during coaxial electrospinning.29 After determining that varying the concentration of PEO in the core solution from approximately 3 to 10 wt.% with negligible improvement in the batches, the solvent was changed from methanol to dichloromethane. Using dichloromethane as the solvent has led to reproducible batches of fibers with SBA-15 fully encapsulated, as shown in Figure 25a. Fibers with fully encapsulated SBA-15 can be seen across the entire batch, as shown by a larger sample of the fibers in Figure 25b. The fibers shown in both SEM images were electrospun at a voltage of 29 a a ) ) b ) b ) a) 16 kV, a flow rate of 0.15 mL/min (for both core and shell solutions), and a collector plate distance of 25 cm.
